public_rationale: TechCrunch reported on May 20, 2025 that Builder.ai was entering insolvency proceedings [e4]. This individual failure does not establish a downturn across model-integrating startup customers [e4]. SimpleClosure's January–June 2026 data cover its own shutdown clients and use a broad AI category [e5]. That sample does not establish a downturn in the specified customer group [e5]. Neither source traces customer distress through revenue losses to greater dependence on big-tech support for survival at OpenAI and Anthropic [e4] [e5]. The evidence therefore leaves the conditional forecast unresolved [e4] [e5].
limitations: The evidence establishes neither the qualifying customer-group downturn nor its consequences for either provider.
It does not show whether startup integrations were either provider's only substantive revenue source.
Matched customer-spending, provider-revenue, liquidity and financing records are missing.
The forecast specifies no deadline or response lag.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If AI startups that integrate these models begin to falter, so will the only real revenue stream OpenAI and Anthropic have, making them more dependent on big tech to keep them alive.
conditions: if AI startups begin to falter

statement.excerpt: If AI startups — by which I mean those companies integrating these models into their apps — begin to falter, so will the only real revenue stream that these companies have, making them more dependent on big tech to keep them alive.

from_speaker: companies integrating these models into their apps
more dependent on big tech to keep them alive
our_interpretation: The model providers referred to are OpenAI and Anthropic.
Read the antecedent as material weakening among the application-startup customer group, rather than an isolated firm's failure. No numerical threshold is supplied.
Read 'only real revenue stream' as the only commercially substantive revenue source, not a denial of every incidental receipt.
The predicted chain is weakening startup customers, weakening provider revenue from those customers, and increased dependence on big-tech support for survival.
The claim has no deadline or specified lag after the triggering downturn.
Revenue and financing must be examined separately. Fundraising alone does not establish survival dependence.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented qualifying downturn, records show that startup integration revenue was the only substantive revenue source for both providers, weakened because of that downturn, and caused greater reliance on big-tech support for survival.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a documented qualifying downturn, sufficiently complete records decisively defeat the predicted chain, including by establishing substantive independent revenue sources and no resulting increase in survival dependence on big tech.

evidence.explanation: This documents an individual AI software company's distress. The report does not establish a broader downturn among customers of the two providers or quantify lost model spending; the company statement is available through this news report.

evidence.locator: Section 'The AI reckoning has not reached the shutdown data'
evidence.explanation: The report covers the company's shutdown clients in the first half of 2026. Its selected sample and broad AI classification cannot establish the condition for the specific application-startup customer group.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence of a qualifying downturn among a consistent cohort of model-integrating startups, followed by sufficiently complete records for each provider. Customer-spending, revenue, liquidity and financing records must establish or decisively defeat the predicted chain, including revenue exclusivity and increased dependence on big-tech support for survival.
